% Appendix F: what Lean checks. The chapter heading is in the main file.
% The table and the numbers come from lean-coverage-data.tex, generated by
% scripts/lean-coverage/make_appendix_f.py from the Lean companion's
% coverage file and receipts (pinned by scripts/lean-coverage/pin_companion.py).

Some steps of this book were also checked in Lean, a proof assistant. They
live in a separate Lean package, the Lean companion, to be released with the
paper. This appendix lists, for each numbered result of the book that the
companion covers, how much of it Lean checks.

The Lean work is still in progress, and the list will become more complete
with time. This appendix records what had been checked by machine at one
fixed version of the companion: commit \lcCommit{}, made on \lcDate{} at
\lcTime{}. All the checks reported below were run on that version, and the
list is generated from its coverage file. A later version may cover more.

Three points apply to every row. First, Lean checks the statements as they
are written in Lean. Second, whether those statements say what the book says
was reviewed by AI models of a different family from the ledger's author; it
has not been checked by a person. Third, the analytic and probabilistic
inputs stay outside Lean: the solution of the stochastic wave equation, the
Stratonovich integrals and the noise, the bounds imported from the
literature, the passage from Laplace transforms to time, and the variational
asymptotics. Where a row says that inputs are supplied, they enter Lean as
named hypotheses.

The last of these reviews covered the results added most recently to the
companion, and its move to the current version of the book: six independent
reviews, whose findings were repaired, and a confirmation review; then, after
the move, a narrow review and a second confirmation review. Their result was
reviewed and accepted by the author; it is still AI-reviewed, not
human-verified.

The companion was built and checked with lean-pkg~\cite{chen:26:lean-pkg},
a tool for registering and checking Lean packages that the author developed
(version~\lcLeanPkgVersion). For commit \lcCommit, lean-pkg records that the
package builds from scratch with no unproved steps, and that every public
declaration, and each of the \lcClaimsChecked{} listed claims, uses only
Lean's three standard axioms (\texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice} and
\texttt{Quot.sound}). A second, separate check confirms that the proofs of
all \lcComparatorTheorems{} theorems prove their statements as restated in a
separate file. The list of claims has \lcVerified{} verified and \lcOpen{}
open. These checks concern the Lean statements themselves; whether those
statements say what the book says is the AI-reviewed match described above.
Most modules were also checked a second time by Lean's separate kernel
checker, run on a computing cluster; the modules added in the last two stages of the work have not yet been
checked this way.
\fi
